mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months in at least 80% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) when GDPC1 YoY change falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 8% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% indicates a restrictive monetary policy environment with weak inflation, which historically coincides with lower risk-free rates and higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy with low inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls below 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% from the previous six-month average signals a contraction in the residential construction sector, which negatively impacts materials and financial firms, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls >10% below 6-month average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) during periods when HOUST declines more than 10% below the prior six-month average for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based slowdown in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) during periods when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate and a fall in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) below the previous six-month average signals accelerating labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS falls below 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) when UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls below the prior six-month average.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the previous twelve-month average for three consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and weaker consumption, which reduces demand for equities and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) during periods when RSAFS exceeds the prior twelve-month average for three consecutive months.
